title: Austria Invoice Requirements & VAT Rates 2026 | Fakturcho
description: Mandatory fields under § 11 UStG 1994, 2026 VAT rates (20/13/10/4.9%), the Kleinunternehmer threshold and Firmenbuch details for invoices issued from Austria.
h1: Invoicing in Austria: mandatory fields, VAT rates and the small-business exemption
answer: An Austrian invoice needs the mandatory fields under § 11 Abs. 1 Z 3 UStG 1994, including a sequential number and, above a gross amount of €10,000 to another business, the recipient's UID number. The standard VAT rate is 20%, alongside 13%, 10% and, from 1 July 2026, a new 4.9% rate for staple foods. A Kleinunternehmer with turnover up to €55,000 a year issues invoices without VAT.

sections.heading: Who must issue an invoice in Austria — and by when?

inline.text: Under § 11 Abs. 1 UStG 1994, an invoice must be issued for a supply to another business for its business or to a legal person, and for taxable Werklieferungen or real-property-related supplies to a private customer. The deadline is
six months
after the supply is made.

Two cases have a shorter deadline: for a service to an EU business where the tax liability shifts to the recipient (Art. 196 MwStSystRL), the invoice is due by the 15th of the month following the supply — the same deadline applies to an intra-Community supply of goods (Art. 11 Abs. 1 BMR).

sections.heading: Mandatory invoice content (§ 11 Abs. 1 Z 3 UStG 1994)

inline.text: A full invoice over €400 (see the small-amount invoice below) needs the following elements:

head: lit.
Mandatory field
rows: Name and address of the supplier
Name and address of the recipient; above a gross amount of €10,000 to another business, also the recipient's UID number
Quantity and trade description, or the type and extent of the service
Date of supply or the supply period (Leistungsdatum — Fakturcho always prints it)
The consideration and the applicable VAT rate, or a note of the exemption
The VAT amount attributable to the consideration
A sequential invoice number, assigned once
The supplier's UID number, except for a Kleinunternehmer or purely input-VAT-exempt supplies

inline.text: Where several rates apply, the consideration and VAT amount must be shown separately per rate (§ 11 Abs. 5 UStG 1994). Where the invoice is in a foreign currency, the VAT amount must also be shown in euro (§ 20 Abs. 6 UStG 1994) — Fakturcho prints a dedicated line with the ECB rate for this.

sections.heading: Small-amount invoice: simplified content up to €400

inline.text: Where the gross total is no more than €400, or the invoice is issued by a Kleinunternehmer, § 11 Abs. 6 UStG 1994 requires only the date of issue, the supplier's name and address, the quantity and description of the supply, the Leistungsdatum, the gross amount with the VAT amount as a single sum, and the VAT rate. The recipient's name and address, the invoice number and the UID number are not required.

Cross-border cases are excluded — intra-Community supplies, reverse-charge supplies to another EU country, and triangulation always need the full invoice. Fakturcho always prints the full invoice regardless; the simplification is purely optional.

head: Rate
Applies to
rows: e.g. art, culture, sports admission, domestic flights (§ 10 Abs. 3, Anlage 2)
e.g. food, books, restaurant meals, residential rent, passenger transport (§ 10 Abs. 2, Anlage 1)
New from 1 July 2026: milk, eggs, certain fruit/vegetables, rice, flour, bread and other staples under Anlage 3 (§ 10 Abs. 1a UStG 1994)

inline.text: Residential letting is taxable at 10%, not exempt (§ 6 Abs. 1 Z 16 UStG 1994 expressly excludes it from the exemption). The earlier 0% rate for photovoltaic modules has expired and no longer applies in 2026.

Special case, Jungholz/Mittelberg: a business with its seat or a permanent establishment in these two municipalities (in Tyrol and Vorarlberg respectively) charges 19% instead of 20% as its standard rate (§ 10 Abs. 4 UStG 1994) — the reduced rates stay the same. Fakturcho offers a dedicated checkbox for this in the issuer profile, pre-ticked from the postcode (6691, 6991, 6992, 6993).

sections.heading: The Kleinunternehmerregelung: up to when is there no VAT?

inline.text: Since 1 January 2025, the Kleinunternehmer exemption under § 6 Abs. 1 Z 27 UStG 1994 applies up to
€55,000 gross turnover

in the preceding and in the current calendar year. If the threshold is exceeded by no more than 10%, the exemption still applies until year end; a larger excess ends it immediately from that supply on.

A Kleinunternehmer issues invoices with no separate VAT shown and needs no UID number for this. Fakturcho automatically prints the note "Umsatzsteuerfrei aufgrund der Kleinunternehmerregelung gemäß § 6 Abs. 1 Z 27 UStG 1994." instead of a VAT line.

Important: if a Kleinunternehmer sells services to a business in another EU country, the place of supply is abroad (§ 3a Abs. 6 UStG 1994) — a UID number is then needed after all, and the reverse-charge rules apply.
Where the tax liability shifts to the recipient (§ 11 Abs. 1a UStG 1994), no VAT may be shown; instead the recipient's UID number and a note of the liability shift must appear. This mainly covers:

items.text: EU B2B services: place of supply at the recipient (§ 3a Abs. 6 UStG 1994), tax owed under Art. 196 MwStSystRL — invoice due by the 15th of the following month, also reported in the EC Sales List (Zusammenfassende Meldung, ZM).
Intra-Community supplies of goods: exempt under Art. 6 Abs. 1 iVm Art. 7 UStG 1994, both UID numbers must appear.

Domestic reverse charge: among others, construction work (§ 19 Abs. 1a), security-transferred goods (§ 19 Abs. 1b), certain electronics/metals (§ 19 Abs. 1d) and mobile phones/emission certificates (§ 19 Abs. 1e).

inline.text: Fakturcho picks the right wording automatically: the Art. 196 wording for cross-border EU services, the selected or a generic § 19 UStG wording for domestic cases, and the Art. 6/7 BMR note for intra-Community supplies of goods.

sections.heading: Company name, Firmenbuch and legal form on business documents (UGB § 14)

inline.text: Every business entered in the Firmenbuch — from a sole trader (e.U.) through an OG or KG to a GmbH — must state its Firma, Rechtsform, Sitz, Firmenbuchnummer and Firmenbuchgericht on business letters addressed to a specific recipient (§ 14 Abs. 1 UGB). An unregistered sole trader (for example below the § 189 UGB accounting thresholds) does not need this — only name and address under § 11 UStG are required.
Fakturcho requires the Firmenbuchgericht and Sitz automatically once a Firmenbuchnummer is entered in the issuer profile, and prints both together with the UID number in the invoice footer.
In Austria, "Gutschrift" is its own legal term: it denotes a document with which the
recipient

of a supply self-bills (§ 11 Abs. 7 UStG 1994), not a later correction by the supplier. A correction document the seller issues itself should therefore never be called "Gutschrift" — Fakturcho calls it "Rechnungskorrektur," or "Stornorechnung" for a full cancellation, and a later additional charge "Nachtragsrechnung" (not the German "Belastungsanzeige").
Every correction references the number and date of the original invoice and states the reason for the correction (§ 11 Abs. 12 UStG 1994).

sections.heading: E-invoicing: who is required to use it in Austria?

inline.text: There is no e-invoicing mandate for B2B or B2C invoices in Austria in 2026; a PDF counts as an electronic invoice once the recipient agrees (§ 11 Abs. 2 UStG 1994). For federal (Bund) contracting authorities (B2G), however, structured e-invoices have been mandatory since 2014, submitted via USP.gv.at or PEPPOL in the ebInterface or Peppol-UBL formats.
From 1 July 2030, structured e-invoicing becomes mandatory for intra-Community B2B supplies under EU Directive 2025/516 (ViDA); no earlier domestic date has been announced so far.
For Austrian invoices, Fakturcho can generate a generic UBL XML file on request; it does not currently offer a dedicated format for submission to federal authorities (ebInterface/PEPPOL).

Invoices must be kept for seven years (§ 11 Abs. 2 UStG 1994, § 132 BAO). The cash-register obligation (§ 131b BAO) only covers cash sales — this also includes card payments made in person, but not bank transfers. Fakturcho is not a cash register and does not replace an RKSV-compliant till for cash payments.

faq.question: Do I need to assign an invoice number as a Kleinunternehmer?

answer.text: Yes. § 11 Abs. 1 Z 3 lit. h UStG 1994 requires a sequential number regardless of whether VAT is shown.

faq.question: Do I always need my customer's UID number?

answer.text: No, only for reverse-charge supplies, intra-Community supplies and triangulation — and for a domestic B2B invoice with a gross amount over €10,000 (§ 11 Abs. 1 Z 3 lit. b UStG 1994).

faq.question: Is a Stornorechnung the same as a Gutschrift?

answer.text: No. In Austria, "Gutschrift" denotes a document with which the customer self-bills. A correction document from the seller is called a Rechnungskorrektur, or a Stornorechnung for a full cancellation.

faq.question: What changes to the VAT rates on 1 July 2026?

answer.text: A new reduced rate of 4.9% applies from that date to certain staple foods such as milk, eggs, bread, flour and rice (§ 10 Abs. 1a UStG 1994).

faq.question: Do I need to be able to issue or receive e-invoices?

answer.text: Not for private business customers; only a supplier to federal authorities must submit structured e-invoices (ebInterface or Peppol-UBL).

faq.question: Does the same VAT rate apply everywhere in Austria?

answer.text: Almost everywhere, yes. Only a business with its seat or a permanent establishment in Jungholz or Kleinwalsertal (Mittelberg) charges 19% instead of 20% as its standard rate (§ 10 Abs. 4 UStG 1994).

body.text: For Austrian issuers, Fakturcho assigns sequential invoice numbers, prints the Leistungsdatum, Firmenbuchnummer, Firmenbuchgericht, Sitz and UID number automatically in the invoice footer, and, for a Kleinunternehmer profile, adds the § 6 Abs. 1 Z 27 UStG 1994 note on its own. For a domestic B2B invoice over €10,000 gross, Fakturcho checks that the recipient's UID number is on file before the invoice can be issued. Businesses in Jungholz or Mittelberg can turn on the special 19% rate in the issuer profile. Fakturcho picks the reverse-charge and intra-Community wording automatically from the destination country and the chosen VAT exemption. As of 29 September 2026.
